size.note: Adults 15-25 cm long when extended (the second-largest slug in the world), 2-3 cm across. The procedural body is 0.18 m from the tail tip to the eyestalk tips, 2.6 cm wide at the foot fringe, the mantle saddle 2.2 cm up; drawn at 0.8-1.2 (animals.js).

source.title: Pacific banana slug (procedural)
source.author: agent (Claude) for Aaron Brodeur
source.original: no mesh: a body of overlapping spheres (the foot fringe, the body, the mantle saddle over the front third, the tapering tail), black blotches, two long eyestalks and two short tentacles (docs/pipeline.md: the gastropod archetype needs no Meshy model)

tiers.note: procedural: one model, no tiers (about 400 triangles); culled beyond 15 m of the eye (animals.js CULL)

rig: procedural (animalModels.js buildSlug, the plain part path): BODY (the foot, body and mantle), TAIL (the rear half, pivot behind the mantle) and HEAD (head and tentacles, pivot at the mantle's front); flick sways the head and eyestalks, pose -1 pulls them in (a touch). Moved by animals.js slUpdate: a crawl of about 4 mm/s in slow curves, long rests with the eyestalks swaying, withdrawn for half a minute when a body comes within 0.5 m; out in cool damp air (the salamanders' rule), under the litter on freezing or hot dry days.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a banana slug at a few metres: olive-yellow with black blotches, a raised mantle, the tapering keeled tail, the two long eyestalks. No slime trail, no keel ridge, no breathing pore; no foot wave (the crawl is a glide of the whole body); the colour is the common yellow form (they range from green-yellow to brown and nearly white).
